A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L2A research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original long- and short-context evaluations, training and inference measurements, pruning experiments, and routing ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds parameter-sharing, runtime-overhead, training-from-scratch, and larger-model pruning experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 introduces an evaluated L2A-shared variant that shares QKVO projections between Local and Global Attention. The default architecture, routing rule, training objective, kernel algorithm, and pruning procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds DCLM training-data coverage through its new from-scratch experiment in Appendix E.1.1. HELMET, BABILong, MRCR, and the short-context evaluation tasks are retained; the added studies introduce no new downstream task families.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 expands the end-to-end training-throughput comparison to include S2-Attn and NSA, whereas v1's corresponding comparison covered L2A and CLP. These methods already participated in accuracy evaluations, whose comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a distinct training-from-scratch protocol: 100B DCLM tokens at 4K context followed by continued pretraining at 128K. Additional experimental controls cover shared projections, 7B pruning at the existing 95% threshold, and 4K/8K kernel timings with preprocessing breakdowns. These expand the experimental design without revising the original training protocol.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic analyses: projection sharing tests parameter duplication, training from scratch tests dependence on pretrained initialization, runtime decomposition examines compaction overhead, and 7B pruning tests scaling beyond 1.5B. The existing routing, window-size, regularization, threshold, and parameter-freezing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Existing sparsity bands and error bars are retained. The new shared-projection discussion invokes externally reported HELMET variability, but adds no uncertainty estimates, run counts, seed information, or statistical tests for the paper's experiments.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and throughput values remain unchanged, including v1 Tables 3–6, now Tables 8–11. New Tables 3–7 report sharing, overhead, from-scratch, and 7B-pruning results; Section 4.2 adds baseline training throughputs. For example, the new scratch-trained models score 11.8 for L2A versus 10.1 for the Transformer at 128K, while 4K kernel speedups range from 0.70× to 1.13× across tested sparsities.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, routing and loss equations, and Appendix A gradient derivation are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and concluding discussion retain the same scientific claims: conditional memory access extends context to 128K while preserving performance, improving efficiency, and enabling KV-cache reduction. The code-release announcement changes access information rather than the core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explains lower sparsity under shared projections as reduced specialization, identifies preprocessing overhead as a limitation at short contexts, and interprets the new experiments as supporting pruning across scales and efficiency when training from scratch. These qualify and extend the existing interpretation without replacing it.

D1.justification: The abstract newly announces an Apache 2.0 code release and repository location. Appendix D.1 clarifies that existing kernel timings include query compaction and index construction, and E.1.1 specifies the new experiment's corpus, token budget, and context schedule. The original Appendix F hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the DCLM citation and a HELMET variability reference. Section 2 newly positions L2A as potentially complementary to key/value sparsification through a two-stage combination. The broader related-work survey and distinction between when and what to retrieve remain intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall section structure are retained. V2 adds localized explanations and a from-scratch ablation subsection, tightens several passages and captions, and updates the conference header and cross-references rather than extensively rewriting the paper.

P2.justification: V2 adds tables displaying projection sharing, runtime components, from-scratch short- and long-context performance, and 7B pruning. It also reorganizes existing displays: the main-text pruning plot moves to Appendix Figure 18, the isolated random-routing figure moves alongside discussion, and window-size plots are resized and grouped together. Existing plotted findings are retained.

improvement.justification: The added controls and preprocessing breakdown strengthen the efficiency evidence and clarify where speedups fail; code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful, bounded gains to an otherwise retained paper. Reporting precision is weakened by a new error: Section 4.2 states a 20.5-point NSA deficit, although Figure 2 reports CLP 40.7 and NSA 21.7, implying 19.0 points.
